reviewMethod: All 20 selected stored files across five current-corpus Organic Letters articles were independently rehashed against the frozen read-only GitHub evidence artifact, checked for exact task/page/article/source DOI identity using the stage binding plus report/index and DOI-bearing article/source URLs, original Figure/Scheme identity and independent caption, captureVersion 6.2.20, job identity, fixed media generation 1790082000000, content-addressed R2 key, actual byte length/type/dimensions, duplicate source/hash ownership and frozen public media-index state. Every SVG was rendered and checked for active/external content. Every image was visually reviewed against its owning caption and paper theme for source role, unrelated/recommendation contamination, duplicate risk and legibility. Capture success/partial markers were treated only as provenance evidence. No publisher request, R2/D1 write, server-side direct import/repair, literature/card/title/scope mutation, userscript change or media-generation change was performed.
quality: The 20 files are exact stored self-contained SVG bytes, all within configured size bounds, all with unique selected full SHA256 and source identities. Frozen public media-index records contain no same-ID body figures for these five DOI; each article has a distinct existing official TOC that is preserved, so this packet is additive and body-only. 10.1021/acs.orglett.6c03389 remains article-level partial 4/5 because Scheme 4 was quality-insufficient; only Scheme 1, Scheme 2, Scheme 3 and Scheme 5 are approved and the missing Scheme 4 is not inferred approved. Historical transport or application/octet-stream fetch failures are retained as provenance and are not attributed to VPN, R2, quota or another cause without evidence.
